title: Sixty paper hats on a table in Bridlington: David Smith and the shape mathematicians had sought for decades

posts.facebook:
A 13-sided shape, cut from card on a table in Bridlington, answered a question mathematicians had asked for decades.

David Smith of Bridlington, a hobbyist with no training in mathematics, found 'the hat': the first single shape known to cover a flat surface only in patterns that never repeat. How he found it, why he could not prove it alone, and the free tools that let you put the same tiles on your own table.

Play with something for long enough to know what normal looks like, and you will notice the day it does something new.

Read the full story → https://dontdieretired.com/think/david-smith-hat-einstein-tile/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=daily
